title: Composition inequality for Bernoulli random restrictions
statement:
Fix $n$, let $E$ be an event on restrictions of $n$ variables, and let $0 < p \le 1$ and $0 < q \le 1$ be real parameters. Then the probability that $E$ holds under a Bernoulli$(pq)$ random restriction is at most the probability, under a Bernoulli$(p)$ random restriction $\rho_1$, that there is some restriction $\rho_2$ for which $E$ holds of the composition of $\rho_1$ with $\rho_2$:
\[
  \Pr_{\rho \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(pq)}\bigl[E(\rho)\bigr]
  \;\le\;
  \Pr_{\rho_1 \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(p)}\bigl[\,\exists\,\rho_2\ :\ E(\rho_1 \circ \rho_2)\,\bigr].
\]
hypotheses_covered: E is an event (decidable predicate) on restrictions of n variables
replaced:
For $0 < p \le 1$ and $0 < q \le 1$, the Bernoulli($pq$) probability of an event is
at most the Bernoulli($p$) probability that some $\rho_2$ makes the event hold after
composition:
\[
  \mathrm{bernoulliRestrProb}\,(pq)\,\mathrm{event}
  \le \mathrm{bernoulliRestrProb}\,p\,\bigl(\rho_1 \mapsto \exists \rho_2,\;
      \mathrm{event}(\mathrm{composeRestr}\,\rho_1\,\rho_2)\bigr).
\]
